title: Inpainting, Outpainting, and Masked Diffusion Editing

questions.question: In inpaint, what does mask[i] == True mean?
options: Dimension i is regenerated by the reverse diffusion chain
Dimension i is copied from clean at every step
Dimension i is removed from the model input
Dimension i is used only as a timestep embedding
questions.explanation: The docstring says True means regenerated; the loop re-noises only positions where `not mask[i]`.

questions.question: With mask=[False,False,False,True,True], which values are described as pinned in main?
options: The last two clean coordinates are copied without any denoising
The first three clean coordinates are kept fixed at the final output
All five coordinates are regenerated independently
Only coordinate 0 is pinned because False is ignored
questions.explanation: The first three False entries are the surrounding context; after reverse sampling the code restores those exact clean values.

questions.question: Why does inpaint re-noise an unmasked coordinate during each reverse timestep?
options: It adds a new mask token to the class embedding
It prevents the network from seeing the clean context at any timestep
It places the known clean value at the current noise level while the masked coordinates are denoised
It converts the clean vector into a one-hot condition
questions.explanation: For `not mask[i]`, the loop sets x[i]=sqrt(alpha_bar)*clean[i]+sqrt(1-alpha_bar)*noise, matching the forward diffusion level before prediction.

questions.question: What does the final `for` loop in inpaint guarantee for unmasked dimensions?
options: They are clipped to the interval [-1,1]
They equal the model's last epsilon prediction
They are replaced with independent Gaussian noise
They equal the original clean values exactly after sampling
questions.explanation: After the reverse loop, every False mask position is assigned `clean[i]`, enforcing exact context preservation.

questions.question: Why is mask=[True,True,False,False,False] used for the outpainting example?
options: It regenerates the head while preserving the tail, extending the sample beyond the known region
It regenerates the tail and copies the head
It masks all five coordinates and samples a new cluster
It changes only the timestep embedding, not x
questions.explanation: The first two True entries are the filled head; the last three False entries form the pinned tail printed by main.

questions.question: What determines the dimensionality of the network input in this lesson?
options: Only t_dim matters because x is regenerated outside the network
The noisy x vector of width d is concatenated with a t_dim timestep embedding, so W1 expects d+t_dim
The mask length replaces the timestep embedding
The number of reverse steps T is concatenated directly to x
questions.explanation: forward builds `inp = list(x_t) + list(t_emb)`, and init_net uses x_dim+t_dim for W1's input width.
